newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Christian network drops "heavy-metal" Pat Boone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Christian network drops "heavy-metal" Pat Boone.

text.p: Singer Pat Boone's musical joke may have backfired -- his gospel show has been taken off the air by a Christian network after he recorded an album of heavy-metal songs and appeared on national television in black leather and a studded dog collar.
The Trinity Broadcasting Network said on Thursday it had dropped Boone's weekly half-hour show after it received thousands of complaints from its viewers.

They were apparently shocked at the sight of the 62-year-old singer at last month's American Music Awards show -- aired on the ABC network -- in black leather, with fake tattoos and a studded choker astride a Harley-Davidson motorcycle.
His appearance was publicity for his new album of heavy-metal classics -- "Pat Boone in a Metal Mood - No More Mr. Nice Guy."

In a recent interview with Reuters, the singer with the squeaky-clean image and Christian outlook had expressed some concern over how his fans might react to him singing what has been called "the devil's music."
But he stressed that the album was part parody and part tribute to a musical genre that was often misunderstood because of the bad image of some of its performers.
He said all he wanted to do was introduce "terrific" songs to an audience that might not normally have heard them.

Trinity Broadcasting, which produces and distributes religious and inspirational Christian programmes through some 400 affiliated TV and radio stations, said it had pulled Boone's show "Gospel America" while executives sought an explanation from Boone about his apparent transformation into a "metal head."

"The decision was based on recent changes in the focus and content of Pat's music, which represents a different genre than the Gospel and traditional inspirational format and ministry of the 'Gospel America' programme," TBN said in a statement.
Boone has accepted an invitation to appear on the network's flagship show "Praise", with its host evangelists Paul and Jan Crouch, to explain his musical metamorphosis.
